summary: Implementation is functionally correct and the SQL/index design is sound, but the PR has multiple style-consistency drifts (handlers reformatted to multi-line while 51 surrounding one-liners stay one-line), a documentation drift between report.md and the actual test inventory (a non-existent dlp.test.js is claimed as 2/2 passed, session.test.js is claimed as 9/9 but has 3 tests), the Test 1 (Migration & Invariant) case from plan §3 is not actually executed, the SKILL.md omits the 2-level flattening depth limit, and ROADMAP.md was not updated to reflect Q-009 resolution. None of these are functional blockers, but together they constitute enough drift that this should not be merged as-is.

findings.problem: The GET handler is reformatted from a single-line arrow body into a multi-line expanded block, breaking the project's consistent one-line handler style used by all 51 other `app.get`/`app.post` calls in the same file.
findings.evidence: `grep -c 'async(req,reply)=>{' apps/server/src/app.ts` returns 51; only the GET (line 241) and POST (line 322) for `/v1/rooms/:roomId/messages` plus the `messageFrom` helper (line 307) use expanded multi-line formatting. The original `app.get("/v1/rooms/:roomId/messages",async(req,reply)=>{...}` was a one-liner before this PR.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the new behavior but compress the handler back to the project one-line arrow style — extract any branches that genuinely do not fit into one line into a named helper to keep handler density.

findings.problem: Same style break as the GET handler — the POST is reformatted multi-line while the surrounding routes are one-line. Inside the body, two near-identical `INSERT INTO inbox_events` statements (lines 384 and 386) duplicate the SQL string verbatim.
findings.evidence: Lines 383-387: only the recipient argument differs between two identical INSERT INTO inbox_events statements. The full SQL string is duplicated.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) compress the POST back to one-line style matching its neighbors, or (b) split into `apps/server/src/threads.ts` exporting `resolveRootThread` and a `notifyAgentInbox` helper — pick one direction.

findings.problem: The reported client test inventory is materially inaccurate: it lists `dlp.test.js: 2/2 passed` (the file does not exist anywhere in the repo or its history) and `session.test.js: 9/9 passed` (the file has 3 tests). It also omits `redaction.test.js (2)` and `state.test.js (6)` from the list. The 41 total is coincidentally correct because the 6 phantom dlp tests balance the 6 missing redaction+state tests.
findings.evidence: `ls packages/client/test/` shows no `dlp.test.js`. `grep -c '^test(' packages/client/test/session.test.js` returns 3. `redaction.test.js` and `state.test.js` exist with 2 and 6 tests respectively but are not in the report.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-list the actual inventory: client.test.js 10, listen-cli.test.js 8, threads.test.js 5, install.test.js 4 (loop), cli.test.js 3, redaction.test.js 2, session.test.js 3, state.test.js 6. Replace the dlp.test.js claim. Total remains 41.

findings.problem: `verification` phase is marked `completed` with timestamp 2026-09-18T00:06:30Z, but the report's per-file test counts are incorrect and the typecheck claim is unverifiable against CI.
findings.evidence: report.md:69-70 asserts `npm run typecheck: 0 errors` across server, web, and client; I confirmed server typechecks but the claim is unbacked for web/client. The verifier wave flagged CI failures prior to this state being written.
findings.suggested_fix: Either revert `verification.status` to `pending` until the corrected test inventory is re-run and a CI run is referenced in report.md, or link the actual CI run URL/screenshot in report.md.

findings.problem: Adds an ECONNREFUSED skip pattern that no other server test (mvp.test.ts, auth-guard.test.ts, embeddings.test.ts, validation.test.ts) uses, creating an inconsistent test runner contract.
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'ECONNREFUSED' apps/server/test/mvp.test.ts` returns no matches. The new test wraps the entire `before` hook in try/catch and the test body in `if (!app) t.skip(...)`. Other server tests assume Postgres is up and fail loudly otherwise.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the skip-and-continue logic to match the existing convention (failing fast is more honest), or apply the same pattern to mvp.test.ts etc. in a separate housekeeping PR.

findings.problem: When `parent.root_message_id !== null` (nested reply), `rootMessageId` is set to `parent.root_message_id` even if the root lookup returns zero rows. The INSERT will then fail with FK violation, surfaced by `setErrorHandler` as 422 `invalid_reference` rather than a clear 400/404.
findings.evidence: Lines 354-363: `} else { rootMessageId = parent.root_message_id; const rootRes = await client.query("SELECT sender_type, sender_id FROM messages WHERE id = $1", [rootMessageId]); if (rootRes.rowCount && rootRes.rows[0].sender_type === "agent") { rootAuthorAgentId = rootRes.rows[0].sender_id; } }`. If `rootRes.rowCount === 0`, `rootMessageId` is still assigned but the INSERT violates the FK.
findings.suggested_fix: After the `rootRes` lookup, add a check for zero rows and return `fail(reply, 422, "invalid_reference", "Reply target's parent thread is missing or has been deleted")` — or simply 400 bad_request.

findings.problem: Plan §3 Test 1 (Migration & Invariant — verify schema supports `root_message_id` and the index `idx_messages_root` exists) is not actually exercised; the test simply uses `root_message_id` end-to-end and assumes the migration worked. The report.md §2.2 claims "covering Tests 1–10b".
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'information_schema\|idx_messages_root' apps/server/test/threads.test.ts` returns no matches. Only `assert.equal(root1Data.root_message_id, null)` style assertions exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit `information_schema.columns` and `pg_indexes` query assertion in setup, or downgrade the report claim to Tests 2–10b.

findings.problem: Q-009 still reads `In progress (jobs/room-threads-2026-09-17)` even though this PR implements the resolution; Q-001 and Q-002 were updated to `✅ Resolved by PR #11` after PR #11 but Q-009 is unchanged.
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'Q-009\|PR #11' docs/ROADMAP.md` shows Q-001/Q-002 with `✅ Resolved by PR #11` but Q-009 status is unchanged from the prior state. The diff is just `2 +/-` lines and shows no edit to row 40.
findings.suggested_fix: Update Q-009's Status cell to `✅ Resolved by PR #12 (2-level flat thread model with implicit thread-author notifications; backward-compatible flat query retained)`.

findings.problem: The new SKILL section does not document the 2-level flat depth limit / flattening semantics that the implementation enforces (Slack/Discord model).
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'depth\|2-level\|two-level\|flatten\|nesting\|nested' skills/olimpyx-participant/SKILL.md` returns zero matches. Plan §1 and PRD §8 #2 call out 2-level flattening.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one bullet: `Thread depth is flat (2 levels): replies to a reply are re-attached to the original root. The server stores reply_to_message_id exactly as given but root_message_id is always the thread root.`

findings.problem: `isRootOnly` and `threadId` are read raw from `req.query as any` without going through any validator. The new code accepts only `q.root_only === "true" || q.root_only === true` and quietly ignores `True`, `1`, `yes`, etc.
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'GET\|query' apps/server/src/validation.ts` returns no GET rows. Line 244: `const isRootOnly = q.root_only === "true" || q.root_only === true;`.

findings.problem: The `messageFrom` helper was previously a one-liner; it's now expanded multi-line. Same style break as the handlers.
findings.evidence: Original `function messageFrom(x:any){return{...}}` was a one-liner. New version is 14 lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore one-line style for `messageFrom` to match the surrounding code conventions.

findings.problem: The LATERAL JOIN is correct but the inner query filters only on `root_message_id`, so the index `idx_messages_root(room_id, root_message_id, created_at)` cannot fully use its leading column for the inner query.
findings.evidence: Index column order is `(room_id, root_message_id, created_at)` while the LATERAL filters only on `r.root_message_id = m.id`. No EXPLAIN ANALYZE is included for Mode B.
findings.suggested_fix: Acceptable as-is. If Mode B becomes hot, add an additional index `ON messages(root_message_id) WHERE root_message_id IS NOT NULL` and include an EXPLAIN assertion in the test.

findings.problem: Two near-identical `INSERT INTO inbox_events` lines and a magic-string `'message.created'` literal — same pattern is used elsewhere in the file.
findings.evidence: `grep -n "'message.created'" apps/server/src/app.ts` shows occurrences at lines 384, 386, 195, and 436 with the same INSERT pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a small helper `notifyInboxEvent(client, agentId, kind, resourceKind, resourceId)` and call it from both message-create branches and the moderation branch.

findings.problem: All logical test cases are crammed into one `test()` block. A failure in Test 2 aborts the entire suite.
findings.evidence: `grep -c '^test(' apps/server/test/threads.test.ts` returns 1 — single block. `mvp.test.ts` also uses 1 block so this is consistent with the codebase convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Either accept the convention since `mvp.test.ts` does the same, or wrap each Test N in `await t.test("Test N: ...", async () => {...})` so failures are isolated.

findings.problem: `client.getThreadMessages(roomId, threadId, { limit, before_cursor: before })` passes `limit` even when undefined; the SDK helper contract isn't explicit about ignoring falsy values.
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'getThreadMessages\|getRoomThreads' packages/client/src/client.js` does not document whether helpers accept `limit: undefined`.
findings.suggested_fix: Spread `{ ...(limit ? { limit } : {}) }` to keep the wire payload minimal, or document in `client.js` that helpers ignore falsy values.

findings.problem: Test uses `password: "password123"` which is 11 characters and would fail registration against `password:z.string().min(12).max(256)` in validation.ts:12.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `password: "very-secure-password-12+chars"` (matches `mvp.test.ts:35` which uses `very secure password`).

assumptions: I treated 'code-style review' as covering both literal style (formatting) and documentation/code consistency, not functional correctness (which was the verifier wave's purview).

I did not actually run `npm test` or `npm run test` — I read source only. The reported client 41/41 passing and the npm run typecheck: 0 errors are taken at the report's word and partially spot-checked (typecheck against apps/server only).
I treated `data.at(-1)!.message_id` non-null assertion as safe because of the prior `data.length === limit` guard — confirmed against the surrounding pattern used in 9 other handlers.

I assumed the report's '5 client tests' means the count of `test()` blocks in `packages/client/test/threads.test.js`, which is correct (5). The report's claim that all 5 are 'real HTTP roundtrips' is partially true: tests 1, 2 use direct SDK calls against an in-process mock server; tests 3-5 spawn the actual CLI subprocess.

I assumed the report's 'Migration passes; column and index exist' claim (Test 1) is satisfied by the schema migration running successfully during `migrate()` — but I did not see an explicit assertion. This is a soft assumption.
